thread:
Maria: Heads-up — sales asked how reserved-pool burst credits behave if a customer downgrades mid-cycle. They want a clear, auditable rule for billing + oncall rollback.
Alex: Clarify: are they asking about committed headroom (reserved pool burst) or soft burst tokens?
Maria: Committed headroom. Also need to cover prewarm instances and active sessions on cancellation.
Jordan: Current behavior drops remaining credits immediately at churn date. That causes surprise errors if active sessions still expect capacity.
Sam: Right. Some customers assume pro-rata refunds or carryover; finance says no refunds in current terms. We need to make behavior explicit.
Priya: From oncall POV, immediate revoke must not take down online traffic. We need a fallback routing path and throttling.
ops-bot: Release deployed: feature/reserved-credit-audit (build 289) to staging at 06:12 UTC.
Maria: Proposed policy: 1) credits remain active until end of billing period unless there's an explicit immediate revoke (fraud/contract breach). 2) No prorated refunds by default. 3) Immediate revokes require ops approval and trigger automated mitigation.
Alex: For immediate revoke mitigation: add a circuit-breaker that 1) notifies oncall, 2) spins a temporary spillover pool, 3) applies a soft-throttle (50% of normal) for 10 minutes, then reevaluate.
Jordan: Need concrete rollback steps in the runbook: a) mark pool expire flag, b) push routing tag to redirect new sessions to fallback model, c) drain long-lived KV caches, d) trigger billing event for customer portal.
Sam: We can implement (b) by letting the routing-service observe pool.metadata.expire=true and selecting fallback variants automatically. Quick to prototype.
Priya: Add alerting: if error rate > 3% or latency spike > 2x baseline within 5 minutes of revoke, escalate to PD.
Maria: How should prewarm be handled? Proposal: prewarm billed as reserved capacity for the remainder of the cycle and stops on revoke with no refund.
Alex: Edge case: customer downgrades to a lower reserved tier but keeps some future commitment — pro-rate the capacity commitment forward (so we reduce future cycles), but keep current cycle credits until its end. That avoids accounting mismatches.
Jordan: Also add audit trails: every credits mutation must write to txn-log and create a human-readable changelog entry and a customer-visible billing event. ops-bot showed txn log rollout to staging. Good start.
Sam: Example internal API to trigger revoke for testing: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/pools/123/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"expire_at":"now"}'```
Priya: Draft oncall playbook steps I'll write up: 1) Trigger revoke flag 2) Push routing-tag and apply throttle policy 3) Start billing-notify job 4) Monitor metrics and PD if thresholds hit 5) Rollback by clearing expire flag and reverting routing rules if failures persist.
Maria: Launch criteria proposed: a) txn logs visible & searchable in staging, b) automated fallback routing passes end-to-end test in staging, c) billing hook emits customer event and shows in UI, d) playbook and owner assigned and PD tested.
Alex: I'll own the staging fallback tests and validate observed behavior.
Jordan: I'll implement audit/event hooks for billing and add changelog entry format.
Sam: I'll spike the routing metadata toggle and throttle enforcement.
Priya: I'll draft and run the oncall PD test in dev.
Maria: Timeline: target rollout before next billing cycle in 2 weeks. If any of the launch criteria fail, gate the rollout.
Alex: Will post progress updates here. :thumbsup:
Maria: Also, I'll check with legal about the no-refund wording for clarity.
Jordan: Linking related support ticket C-9032 for context (customer complained about surprise loss of burst mid-cycle).
Sam: Noted and will reference in the PR.
Priya: Playbook draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/dedicated/reserved-revoke-playbook (will update with PD run results).
Maria: Action items: Alex (staging tests), Jordan (audit + billing events), Sam (routing + throttle), Priya (playbook + PD). Check back in 48h with status.
